subject: Re: Data retention discussion — Acme requirements and options
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>

Subject: Data retention discussion — Acme requirements and options

Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to understand Acme's security posture and the specific retention constraints for the customer-facing features you're prototyping. Quick recap and next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what I heard from you:
- Need strong safeguards around PII and request payloads (PII must not be stored persistently).
- Preference for a 0-retention model for customer request bodies where feasible; otherwise, a very short retention window (<=24 hours) for logs.
- Audit logs for access must be available to your security team, but ideally encrypted with your KMS.
- You expect the DPA and any retention exceptions to be reviewed by legal/security before procurement signs off.

What Redwood can do (high level):
- We have options across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments that affect retention guarantees.
- We can provide an exception path for shortened/zero retention for request payloads; there are tradeoffs for debugging, replay, and quality monitoring which we explain in the attached Data_Retention_Matrix.xlsx.
- We can store audit logs outside the default retention (customer-managed bucket + KMS) as part of an enterprise agreement.

Attachments: Data_Retention_Matrix.xlsx (matrix of options + technical tradeoffs), DPA_redwood_v2.docx (redlined DPA).

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll loop in Marissa (solutions engineer) to confirm technical feasibility and any constraints for a 0-retention config on the Hosted path vs. Dedicated/Private.
2) If the hosted path can meet a 0-retention SLA for request payloads, Rafael and I will surface any commercial uplift and add it to the quote.
3) We can route the DPA to your legal once we align on the retention option — please share the contact for legal and security reviewers if different from this thread.

Can you confirm if 24 hours is the maximum you could accept if zero retention is not possible for hosted? Also please share your legal point of contact so we can route the DPA.

Thanks — happy to jump back on a short call if that makes it easier.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Data retention discussion — Acme requirements and options

Hi Lauren — looping in Marissa (solutions engineer) here — quick technical write-up below + pointers to the attached matrix.

On zero retention vs ephemeral: 
- Zero-retention (as a contractual promise) means Redwood will not persist request payloads to long-term storage. Practically, that can be implemented in two ways depending on deployment model: 
  * Hosted (shared control plane): we can configure request payloads to be discarded immediately after response processing (ephemeral in-memory handling) and avoid writing them to logs or disk. This limits debugging and replay — only transient traces for live debugging (with customer's approval) would be available and they would not be stored persistently.
  * Dedicated/Private: for an enterprise private deployment we can completely disable request-body logging and route audit logs to your customer-managed S3 bucket with customer KMS encryption. This gives the strongest contractual guarantees.

On shortened logs (24h window):
- For hosted, we can tier a retention profile that retains request payloads for a configurable window (24h, 72h, 7d). Shorter windows reduce debugging/monitoring ability (root cause and model quality regression analysis). Our suggested default if you need minimal operational visibility is 24 hours.

On audit logs and KMS: 
- We support delivering audit logs into a customer-managed storage location encrypted with your KMS keys (we accept AWS KMS/CloudHSM, GCP KMS, or vault HSM integrations). Retention for audit logs can be set independently (you requested 7 years — feasible for Dedicated/Private with appropriate contractual terms).

Tradeoffs / caveats:
- Billing and usage aggregation metrics: we must retain aggregate billing metrics for invoicing; these do not contain raw PII but will include token counts and timestamps. We can minimize fields retained.
- Debugging: with strict zero-retention we will have limited ability to reproduce customer issues without engaging a live session or obtaining explicit temporary debug consent from your team.
- SLA for zero-retention: We can include a contractual exception to guarantee zero-persistence of request payloads for the hosted path, but it will require an addendum specifying acceptable debug procedures and a small commercial uplift to cover the operational overhead and reduced telemetry.

Costs and commercial note:
- Rafael and Camila will follow up on pricing. Ballpark: customers who require a zero-retention SLA on hosted typically see a 10-18% uplift depending on support/retention of audit logs. Dedicated/Private pricing is quoted separately.

Attached: Data_Retention_Matrix.xlsx (detailed mapping of deployment vs retention vs tradeoffs), DPA_redwood_v2.docx (redline).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Camila/Rafael: provide a brief SOW addendum option with 0-retention hosted add-on and estimated uplift.
2) Lauren/Acme: confirm legal contact (Lauren's provided) and whether you want the audit logs delivered to a customer-managed bucket (please share the desired cloud provider).

Happy to hop on a call with your security team to walk through the matrix tomorrow if needed.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
